sections.title: Right now
lines: Pre-race growth. Green flag Sun 10/18 2:00 PM CT (in 3d 12h).
Sold 10,835 contracts so far; 56,256 more resting on the book. Premium collected $1,263.
Worst line is -$1,137. The glide target right now is -$800, so it is $337 short; the final target is -$200 by T-60.
Backstop is ON for Denny Hamlin, Joey Logano: their lines are under -$800, so they stop adding until the others catch up.
Prices follow Bovada, refreshed every 5m (last 4m ago). Covers 37 of 37 drivers.

New posts are on hold: free cash is $1,246 (read 2m ago) and this book keeps $1,300 free before it posts anything new. Orders already on the book stay. The hold lifts by itself once cash is back over $1,300.

sections.title: Lagging sides
lines: Kyle Larson: sold 0, 2,400 behind the leader. Cheapest row 10c; the crowd has been buying at 10c; fair 7.9c. Already at its floor (about 10c); it will not go lower unless the crowd price or fair drops.

Christopher Bell: sold 900, 1,500 behind the leader. Cheapest row 19c; the crowd has been buying at 19c; fair 15.6c. Already at its floor (about 19c); it will not go lower unless the crowd price or fair drops.

Ryan Blaney: sold 1,745, 655 behind the leader. Cheapest row 20c; the crowd has been buying at 20c; fair 20.2c. Already at its floor (about 20c); it will not go lower unless the crowd price or fair drops.

Chase Briscoe: sold 1,851, 549 behind the leader. Nothing is resting on it: new posts are on hold: free cash $1,246 is under the $1,300 floor; its rows vanished with no fill 26m ago and the bot re-posted them.

The bot checks every 30s; it logs a market snapshot every 10 min. Rows already resting are not repriced when the sportsbook moves; only new rows use the fresh price. A step is skipped if filling the new row in full would push a line under the backstop or the glide target.
From T-360 (glide start) the price-step rule is on for lagging drivers so they can sell into the late rush of crowd orders.

sections.title: Next wave of contracts
lines: Trigger: when a driver's current wave is 90% filled and a full fill would keep his line above the gate, the bot posts the next wave (sizes 2,000/1,500/1,500 for contenders/midfield/long shots per wave), priced one cent above the last fill. The book's worst line must also be above the backstop, and free cash above the $1,300 floor.
Right now it is the growth phase (before T-360): the gate is loose (-$2,000) and the number of contracts is limited by what the crowd is likely to buy and by free cash.
Josh Berry: 2 waves so far, 2,440 contracts offered in all; the latest (940 at 3c) is 0% filled.
Waves stop at T-60.

sections.title: Tightening
lines: The risk glide starts at T-360 (Sun 10/18 8:00 AM CT, in 3d 6h). Until then the limit on the worst line is the backstop (-$800). From then the limit slides in a straight line to -$200 at T-60 (Sun 10/18 1:00 PM CT).

When the worst line is under the target the bot: blocks any post whose full fill would break the target, shrinks resting size over the room in place, buys back the worst line cheaply (only when each dollar spent lifts the line 2.0x or more, up to 3 per loop, budget 50% of banked premium), and starts selling to close gaps from T-90.
Preview: if the worst line is still -$1,137 at T-360, the glide would have to bring it up by about $337 to reach the first target.
Even-up (lagging drivers re-priced to fair) from T-60; the take window (sell to close gaps) from T-20 to the green flag.
Checkpoints: T-2880, T-1440, T-360, T-180, T-120, T-60, T-20 before the green flag.
At the green flag the bot keeps the resting orders and hands over to the in-race engine.

sections.title: Will it adapt on its own?
lines: Yes, on its own: new waves for popular drivers, price steps on lagging contenders, the backstop that stops a heavy driver, and the glide that tightens the worst line toward -$200.

No, it will not: reprice a resting row when Bovada moves, or buy back a driver for any reason except the glide's cheap-lift rule. If Bovada's field drops below 80% coverage the bot just holds what it has.

The one thing that depends on the market: the worst line is -$1,137 against a -$200 final target. Premium from the rest of the field and fills on lagging drivers lift it; the glide's buybacks cover what is left, within their budget. It might not fully close.
I only read the bot's settings, state and log. I cannot see its next decision, only the rules it follows.
